status: Accepted working sequence under W4-012; detailed field bounds and implementation briefs remain to be selected. Dependencies are minimum logical dependencies, not a strict serial schedule.

variations.title: Build a useful MIDI sketch
variations.task: Use current drum, bass, melodic, or harmonic material supplied by the user. Edit rhythm, pitches, lengths, and velocities, then make a contrasting section with existing devices. Resolve at least one device, plug-in, or Bitwig preset by name rather than by explicit ID.
variations.acceptance: The two sections contain the intended notes and sound choices. Unedited notes and tracks retain their required state. Use existing MIDI/document paths first. A named device or preset resolves to one exact identity, from the native catalog or through R05 browser discovery, and the inserted device is confirmed independently.
variations.limit: Current note, MIDI-file, and device tools are the starting point. No new notation, pressure route, or deep container is a prerequisite. Browser discovery is unproved (E101); if R05 fails, name resolution falls back to the offline native catalog and explicit VST3/CLAP IDs.

variations.title: Edit difficult MIDI without hidden loss
variations.task: Use expressive multichannel material with pickups, tuplets, same-pitch overlaps, long notes, and loop offsets. Change selected notes without rewriting unrelated expression.
variations.acceptance: Each field has an independent read/write/preservation verdict. Unsupported edits report a precise limit. Pressure receives a corrected route, a reproducible defect report, or an explicit unresolved condition.
variations.limit: Readback has timing and pressure limits. Do not use a lossy projection as a fidelity oracle. An upstream response must not block other MIDI work.

variations.title: Arrange and revise song sections
variations.task: Read the Arranger, place MIDI sections, duplicate a chorus, move a passage, and change clip start, loop, and play ranges. Optionally read and create cue markers for the song sections.
variations.acceptance: The intended sections occur at the required musical times. Notes, offsets, overlaps, tempo/meter interpretation, and neighboring clips meet the selected preservation rules. If cue markers are used, each marker has the intended name and position.
variations.limit: Prove exact Arranger reads before writes. Launcher performance recording is optional later work, not an equivalent timeline editor. Cue markers (SM-5) are optional scope; only tempo, meter, and position verbs of SM-4 are required.

variations.title: Shape the arrangement with automation
variations.task: Add a filter rise and volume transition. Read and edit points and curves, then move a passage with its required automation.
variations.acceptance: Target, timing, values, and curve behavior match the intended transition. Untouched lanes stay intact. Distinguish clip and Arranger automation.
variations.limit: Start with one useful lane and expand by model. Do not infer all automation types from one passing curve.

variations.title: Edit existing audio as song material
variations.task: Read an existing audio clip, identify its source and range, insert another, trim or split a section, move/duplicate it, replace its source where needed, and delete an owned clip.
variations.acceptance: The selected create/read/update/delete verbs preserve source identity, timing, audible content, and neighboring clips. Include Launcher and Arranger cases where their models differ.
variations.limit: CA-8 has no surveyed read route. Prove that read before dependent edits. Warp/stretch is a later audio-depth case if the selected song needs it.

variations.title: Put externally sliced hits into a drum instrument
variations.task: Accept hit files from an external splicer. Create or use drum pads and Samplers, assign hits, read or retrieve their sources, then replace or clear a sample. Set only the required region/playback fields.
variations.acceptance: The intended pads use the correct sources and ranges. Sample retrieval returns a usable reference or file where supported. Replacement and clearing preserve unrelated pad/device state. Slicing and analysis stay external.
variations.limit: Insertion does not prove source retrieval or clearing. Embedded sample extraction needs route proof. Advanced multisample, wavetable, and arbitrary plugin sample state are not initial requirements.

variations.title: Read back one track for external analysis
variations.task: Read back one existing clip through its track devices, before the track fader, over the full clip or a measure/two. Produce an inaudible bounded audio artifact for external sound-design analysis.
variations.acceptance: Verify post-device/pre-fader signal scope, file identity, range, channels, and stated tail/routing limits. Prove inaudibility and measure end-to-end latency. Final export and recording stay operator tasks.
variations.limit: The desired bounce route is not proved. R03 resolves sends, sidechains, tails, and fallback only as needed. Source extraction is not processed audio readback.

variations.title: Make the song sound playable
variations.task: Take a sound used in the song. Choose useful controls, set performance ranges, and create the remote mappings needed to play it.
variations.acceptance: Named controls reach the intended parameters over useful ranges. Mapping edits preserve the rest of the chain. Operator save/export is acceptable.
variations.limit: DP-2 needs live route assessment. Physical-unit input, nesting, and preset export are dependencies only when this instrument needs them.

variations.title: Author and revise live modulation
variations.task: Add a useful modulator and mapping to that sound. Change amount, enable/mode, source, or curve only as the musical variation requires.
variations.acceptance: Independent state and a bounded functional check show the intended modulation. Change or remove the mapping without unrelated changes. Record each live setter verdict.
variations.limit: Use external implementations as leads. Grid mappings, outer modulators, and remote pages are separate surfaces. Keep a working file route until a replacement passes.

variations.title: Construct a useful Grid instrument
variations.task: Run Phase 11 read/catalog work, then build or extend a Poly Grid voice. Edit modules, values, cables, and internal mappings for one useful sound.
variations.acceptance: Read the resulting graph independently, exercise the sound, and preserve existing module positions. Required save/reopen behavior holds for this instrument.
variations.limit: Keep Phase 11 scope, cost model, admitted roles, and session order. Mapping amount uses remove/re-add. This branch can advance while outer-modulator work is blocked.

variations.title: Extend Grid where it changes the instrument
variations.task: Try the next useful integer/indexed value, relocation, stateful attachment, or FX/Note Grid variation. Expand supported modulation by musical need.
variations.acceptance: Each added field or family has its own proved result, preservation rule, and stated limit. Stop after the useful instrument is achieved or the bounded route fails.
variations.limit: GI-2 is mixed proof. Resources, arrays, large patches, rare device state, and DSP changes are separate proposals, not automatic completion requirements.

variations.title: Balance the completed arrangement
variations.task: Set levels and pan, create the Effect track that a send needs, add one useful send, set track arm/active state or colour where the mix needs them, and adjust the required Master controls and processing. Use mix automation from V04.
variations.acceptance: The intended mixer and device state is read back. Effect-track creation is measured and the add_tracks description is corrected in this case. Only routing, groups, or returns needed by this mix are promoted. The operator handles final export.
variations.limit: SM-2/3 are distinct from basic track mixing. SM-7 is limited to Effect-track creation for sends; Group and Hybrid tracks remain bonus work. SM-1 covers only the track fields the mix uses. Do not make general routing, live launching, or automated stem export prerequisites.

variations.title: Polish and compare a mix revision
variations.task: Change the required stock/plugin processing, then compare the relevant track readback or operator-provided mix export through external analysis.
variations.acceptance: The intended processing changes and audio provenance are clear. The operator can save and export the finished result. External judgments do not replace structural readback.
variations.limit: Reuse V07 when it meets the requested scope. Do not grow this into unattended recording, all-stem rendering, or a new analysis provider.

inputPolicy: Workflow templates: the user supplies current real material at execution. Ask material acceptance questions when implementing the affected capability.
